newsitem.title: INDONESIA: U.S. confirms it will take Indonesia to WTO.
newsitem.headline: U.S. confirms it will take Indonesia to WTO.

text.p: The United States confirmed on Friday it would take Indonesia to the World Trade Organistion (WTO) over its controversial car policy forming a united front with Japan and the European Union.
"In the last few days, we have identified the national car policy as a problem," deputy U.S. Trade Representative Jeffrey Lang told a news conference.
"We are going to use the WTO, not domestic trade laws," Lang said during a one-day visit to discuss telecommunications deregulation ahead of the December WTO meeting in Singapore.

He said Washington would first enter consultations with Jakarta within the WTO and if these were not successful it would then take the matter to a WTO arbitration panel. This could then be appealed, he said.

"This whole process can take 13 to 15 or 16 months and we are at the very beginning of the consultative process. We are hopeful the matter can be resolved before it has to enter other steps," Lang said.

The United States, Japan and the European Union have opposed the national car policy which gives tax and tariff breaks to a joint venture between one of President Suharto's sons and Kia Motors of South Korea.
"It is obvious that the programme discriminates against the import of automobiles and conditions of investment and both of those things are obviously inconsistent (with) the WTO," he said.
Lang said the United States was not yet considering trade retaliation under its 301 trade law.
"If we're required to retaliate we might have to use 301 but that is....hypothetical at this stage," he said.
